_meta.description: Real spatial transcriptomics platforms and their properties. Drives which pipeline steps are required (e.g. spot-based platforms need deconvolution; imaging-based platforms need cell segmentation).

visium.name: 10x Visium
visium.resolution: 55 um spots, 100 um center-to-center; each spot captures 1-10 cells
visium.notes: Spots are multi-cellular, so 'cell typing' is really deconvolution (estimating cell-type proportions per spot). Do NOT report per-cell types from raw Visium spots.
visium.known_limits: Not single-cell. Spot composition confounds spatial DE and cell-cell communication inference.

visium_hd.name: 10x Visium HD
visium_hd.resolution: 2 um bins (continuous lawn), commonly analyzed at 8 um or 16 um binning
visium_hd.typical_units_per_sample: millions of 2um bins; ~100k-500k cells after binning/segmentation
visium_hd.notes: 2um bins approach single-cell but are not cells. Use bin2cell (nucleus-expansion via StarDist/Cellpose on the H&E) or bin aggregation to build cell objects. Very large: expect memory pressure.
visium_hd.known_limits: Bin-to-cell assignment is an active, imperfect area. 2um bins are sparse; naive per-bin clustering is noisy.

xenium.name: 10x Xenium
xenium.notes: Ships with a default (nucleus-expansion / multimodal) segmentation, but re-segmentation with Baysor/Cellpose/ProSeg often improves boundaries. Panel is targeted, so untargeted cell types may be unresolvable.
xenium.known_limits: Limited gene panel caps annotation granularity. Segmentation errors propagate into every downstream count.

merscope.name: Vizgen MERSCOPE (MERFISH)
merscope.notes: Vizgen provides Cellpose-based cell boundaries; transcript-based re-segmentation (Baysor/ProSeg) is common. DAPI + poly-T + membrane stains available for segmentation.
merscope.known_limits: Optical crowding in dense tissue causes transcript mis-assignment. Targeted panel limits annotation.

cosmx.name: NanoString CosMx SMI
cosmx.notes: Higher plex than Xenium/MERSCOPE (esp. WTx). Default segmentation via CellPose on IF morphology markers. Background/false-positive counts are non-trivial; use negative-probe QC.
cosmx.known_limits: Higher background than other imaging platforms; aggressive negative-probe filtering needed. Segmentation quality varies by tissue.

stereo_seq.name: Stereo-seq (BGI STOMICS)
stereo_seq.resolution: 220-500 nm DNB spots (nanoscale), analyzed at binned resolution (bin20/bin50) or cell-segmented
stereo_seq.typical_units_per_sample: very large FOV (cm-scale); millions of DNBs; 100k-1M+ cells after segmentation
stereo_seq.notes: Nanoscale DNBs are sub-cellular; bin into squares (bin50 ~25um) or segment cells with the ssDNA/nuclei image (Cellpose, StarDist, or Stereopy Cell Segmentation). Huge FOV enables whole-organ sections.
stereo_seq.known_limits: Enormous data volume (memory/compute). Cell segmentation from ssDNA is imperfect; bin-based analysis is a common compromise but is not single-cell.
